narrative:
The model estimated a 58% chance that you would be a bad credit risk, so your application was denied because this predicted risk exceeded the bank’s approval threshold. That does not mean repayment is certain to fail; it means the information provided looked somewhat more like borrowers who had difficulty than like approved applicants.

By far the strongest factor was your checking account status: being below zero DM. Only about 12.6% of approved applicants had this status, and it pushed the decision toward bad credit. The second most important factor was your property position: no known property or assets. That is uncommon among approved applicants, at about 7.8%, and it also pushed toward bad credit. Your installment burden worked in your favor: at 2% of disposable income, it is below the approved average of about 2.99%, suggesting a lighter repayment load and pushing toward good credit. However, that positive factor was not enough to outweigh the checking-account and property concerns.

To improve your position, bring your checking account into positive standing and keep it there for several months. Document any assets, collateral, or a suitable guarantor, and consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter term to reduce risk. Ask the lender what specific evidence would support a new application, then reapply once those points are stronger.
